'''Masataka Nakazawa''' (born 17 September 1952) is a Japanese researcher in optical communication engineering. He is a [[distinguished professor]] at [[Tohoku University]] in Japan.<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |title=The Japan Prize Foundation – The 2023 Japan Prize |url=https://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_prof_2023_nakazawa.html |access-date=2023-03-07 |website=The Japan Prize Foundation |archive-date=2023-03-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308082559/https://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_prof_2023_nakazawa.html |url-status=live }}</ref> His pioneering work on [[EDFA|erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA)]] has made a significant contribution to the development of global long-distance, high-capacity optical fiber network.<ref name="bio"/>

== Biography ==
Masataka Nakazawa received B.S. in Electronics from [[Kanazawa University]] in 1975, M.S. in Physical Electronics from [[Tokyo Institute of Technology]] in 1977, and Ph.D. in Applied Electronics from Tokyo Institute of Technology in 1980.<ref name="bio" /> After receiving a Ph. D. degree, he joined the Electrical Communication Laboratory of [[Nippon Telegraph and Telephone|Nippon Telegraph & Telephone Public Corporation]] in 1980.<ref name="bio" /> He was a visiting scientist at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1984.<ref name="bio" /> In 1999, he became an NTT R&D Fellow.<ref name="bio" /> Then, in 2001, he moved to the [[Research Institute of Electronic Communication|Research Institute of Electrical Communication (RIEC)]] at Tohoku University. He became a distinguished professor (DP) in 2008 and the director of RIEC in 2010.<ref name="bio" /> He also served as the director of Japan Council for Research Institutes and Centers of National Universities and of Research Organization of Electrical Communication (ROEC) in 2011.<ref name="bio" /> Currently, he is a director of Kanazawa University (part time) and a specially appointed professor/ distinguished professor at the International Research Institute of Disaster Science at Tohoku University<ref name="bio" />

== Research ==
He introduced [[erbium]] ions into optical communication in 1984, when he constructed the first erbium (Er<sup>3+</sup>): [[Solid-state laser|glass laser]] operating at 1.55 μm,<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Y. |last1=Morishige |first2=S. |last2=Kishida |first3=K. |last3=Washio |first4=H. |last4=Toratani |first5=M. |last5=Nakazawa |title=Output-stabilized high-repetition-rate 1.545-μm Q-switched Er:glass laser |journal=Optics Letters |volume=9 |issue=5 |pages=147–149 |year=1984 |doi=10.1364/OL.9.000147|pmid=19721525 }}</ref> and then used it as an [[optical time domain reflectometer]] (OTDR). This enabled a fault to be located in a 130&nbsp;km-long single-mode fiber, which remains the world record distance.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=M. |last2=Tokuda |first3=K. |last3=Washio |first4=Y. |last4=Asahara |title=130-km long fault location for single-mode optical fiber using 1.55 μm Q-switched Er<sup>3+</sup>: glass laser |journal=Optics Letters |volume=9 |issue=7 |pages=312–314 |year=1984 |doi=10.1364/ol.9.000312|pmid=19721581 }}</ref> He then began research on an erbium-doped [[fiber laser]] in 1987<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=Y. |last2=Kimura |title=Simultaneous oscillation at 0.91, 1.08, 1.53 μm in a fusion-spliced fiber laser |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=51 |pages=1768–1770 |year=1987|issue=22 |doi=10.1063/1.98516 }}</ref> and [[amplifier]] in 1989.<ref name="EDFA">{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=Y. |last2=Kimura |first3=K. |last3=Suzuki |title=Efficient Er<sup>3+</sup>-doped optical fiber amplifier pumped by a 1.48 μm InGaAsP laser diode |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=54 |pages=295–297 |year=1989|issue=4 |doi=10.1063/1.101448 }}</ref> After Dr. [[Robert J. Mears|R. J. Mears]] of [[David N. Payne|Prof. Payne’s group]] reported the first [[EDFA]] in 1987,<ref>{{cite journal |first1=R. J. |last1=Mears |first2=L. |last2=Reekie |first3=I. M. |last3=Jauncy |first4=D. N. |last4=Payne |title=Low-noise erbium-doped fibre amplifier operating at 1.54 mm |publisher=IEE |journal=Electronics Letters |volume=23 |issue=19 |pages=1026–1028 |year=1987|doi=10.1049/el:19870719 |bibcode=1987ElL....23.1026M |url=https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/78511/1/304.pdf }}</ref> Dr. Nakazawa used a [[InGaAsP|1.48 μm InGaAsP]] [[laser diode]] (LD) to pump the erbium fiber<ref name="EDFA" /> and reported the highest gain of 46.5&nbsp;dB in 1989<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Y. |last1=Kimura |first2=K. |last2=Suzuki |first3=M. |last3=Nakazawa |title=46.5 dB gain in Er<sup>3+</sup>-doped fibre amplifier pumped by 1.48 μm GaInAsP laser diodes |journal=Electronics Letters |volume=25 |pages=1656–1657 |year=1989|issue=24 |doi=10.1049/el:19891110 |bibcode=1989ElL....25.1656K }}</ref> after employing the LD for [[Raman amplification]] at 1.55 μm in 1988.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=K. |last1=Suzuki |first2=M. |last2=Nakazawa |title=Raman amplification in P2O5 doped silica fibers |journal=International Quantum Electronics Conference |location=Tokyo, Japan |year=1988 |pages=MP43 |url=https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?uri=IQEC-1988-MP43}}</ref> He invented the LD pumped erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA),<ref name="EDFA" /> which made it possible to construct a compact, reliable, and low-power consumption optical repeater for high-speed, high-capacity, and long-distance optical communication systems. He also reported [[Raman amplification|backward Raman amplification]] in 1984,<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=M. |last2=Tokuda |first3=Y. |last3=Negishi |first4=N. |last4=Uchida |title=Active transmission line: Light amplification by backward stimulated Raman scattering in polarization-maintaining optical fiber |journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America B |volume=l |issue=1 |pages=80–85 |year=1984 |doi=10.1364/JOSAB.1.000080|bibcode=1984JOSAB...1...80N }}</ref> which remains in commercial use.

He subsequently undertook intensive work on high-speed optical transmission technology using ultrashort [[Gaussian function|Gaussian pulses]],<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=T. |last2=Yamamoto |first3=K.R. |last3=Tamura |title=1.28 Tbit/s–70 km OTDM transmission using third- and fourth-order simultaneous dispersion compensation with a phase modulator |publisher=IEE |journal=Electronics Letters |volume=36 |issue=24 |pages=2027–2029 |year=2000 |doi=10.1049/el:20001391|bibcode=2000ElL....36.2027N }}</ref> [[optical solitons]],<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=Y. |last2=Kimura |first3=K. |last3=Suzuki |title=Soliton amplification and transmission with Er<sup>3+</sup>-doped fibre repeater pumped by GaInAsP laser diode |journal=Electronics Letters |volume=25 |issue=3 |pages=199–200 |year=1989 |doi=10.1049/el:19890143|bibcode=1989ElL....25..199N }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=K. |last2=Suzuki |first3=Y. |last3=Kimura |title=3.2-5 Gb/s, 100 km error-free soliton transmission with erbium amplifiers and repeaters |journal=IEEE Photonics Technology Letters |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=216–219 |year=1990 |doi=10.1109/68.50894|bibcode=1990IPTL....2..216N |s2cid=7735296 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=E. |last2=Yamada |first3=H. |last3=Kubota |first4=K. |last4=Suzuki |title=10 Gbit/s soliton data transmission over one million kilometres  |journal=Electronics Letters |volume=27 |issue=14 |pages=1270–1272 |year=1991 |doi=10.1049/el:19910796|bibcode=1991ElL....27.1270N }}</ref> optical [[Fourier transformation]],<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=T. |last2=Hirooka |title=Distortion-free optical transmission using time-domain optical Fourier transformation and transform-limited optical pulses |journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America B |volume=22 |issue=9 |pages=1842–1855 |year=2005 |doi=10.1364/JOSAB.22.001842|bibcode=2005JOSAB..22.1842N }}</ref> and [[Harry Nyquist|Nyquist pulses]].<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=T. |last2=Hirooka |first3=P. |last3=Ruan |first4=P. |last4=Guan |title=Ultrahigh-speed "orthogonal" TDM transmission with an optical Nyquist pulse train |journal=Optics Express |volume=20 |issue=2 |pages=1129–1140 |year=2012 |doi=10.1364/OE.20.001129|pmid=22274458 |bibcode=2012OExpr..20.1129N |doi-access=free }}</ref> Nakazawa’s work spans diverse areas of photonics including optical communication, various [[fiber laser]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=E. |last2=Yoshida |first3=Y. |last3=Kimura |title=Ultrastable harmonically and regeneratively modelocked polarisation-maintaining erbium fibre ring laser |journal=Electronics Letters |volume=30 |issue=19 |pages=1603–1604 |year=1994 |doi=10.1049/el:19941072|bibcode=1994ElL....30.1603N }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=K. |last1=Kasai |first2=M. |last2=Yoshida |first3=M. |last3=Nakazawa |title=Acetylene (13C2H2) stabilized single-polarization fiber laser |journal=IEICE Trans. Electron. |volume=J88-C |issue=9 |pages=708–715 |date=September 2005}}</ref> and [[quadrature amplitude modulation]] (QAM) [[coherent transmission]] with the highest multiplicity of 4096.<ref>{{cite book |first1=M. |last1=Terayama |first2=S. |last2=Okamoto |first3=K. |last3=Kasai |first4=M. |last4=Yoshida |first5=M. |last5=Nakazawa |chapter=4096 QAM (72&nbsp;Gbit/s) single-carrier coherent optical transmission with a potential SE of 15.8 bit/s/Hz in all-Raman amplified 160 km fiber link|title=Optical Fiber Communications Conference and Exposition (OFC) |pages=1–3 |year=2018 |chapter-url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8386225 |isbn=978-1-943580-38-5}}</ref> Recently, he has been concentrating on [[Mode locking]] technology for the generation of various optical pulses<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |first2=T. |last2=Hirooka |title=Theory of FM Mode-Locking of a Laser as an Arbitrary Optical Function Generator |journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics |volume=58 |issue=2 |pages=1–25 |year=2022 |doi=10.1109/JQE.2022.3143521|bibcode=2022IJQE...5843521N |s2cid=245968790 }}</ref> and a QAM quantum noise stream cipher with continuous variable [[quantum key distribution]] (QKD).<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Nakazawa |display-authors=etal |title=QAM Quantum Noise Stream Cipher Transmission Over 100 km With Continuous Variable Quantum Key Distribution  |journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics |volume=53 |issue=4 |pages=1–16 |year=2017 |doi=10.1109/JQE.2017.2708523|bibcode=2017IJQE...53E8523N |s2cid=39497552 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
 
He has published more than 500 academic journal papers<ref name="ieee" /> and given 400 international conference presentations. During his 40-year career he has received 5 paper awards and three centennial milestone certificates of commendation<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieice.org/jpn_r/publication/milestone.html|title=電子情報通信学会マイルストーン &#124; 一般社団法人 電子情報通信学会|website=www.ieice.org|access-date=2023-03-08|archive-date=2023-03-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308082554/https://www.ieice.org/jpn_r/publication/milestone.html|url-status=live}}</ref> from the [[Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers|Institute of Electronics, Information, and Communication Engineers (IEICE)]].

== Professional society membership ==
He is a Fellow and Honorary Member of the [[Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers|Institute of Electronics, Information, and Communication Engineers (IEICE)]],<ref name="ieice">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieice.org/eng/about_ieice/new_honorary_members_award_winners/2017/meiyo_04e.html|title=Masataka NAKAZAWA &#124; Honorary Member &#124; New Honorary Members, Award Winners in 2017 &#124; IEICE The Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers|website=www.ieice.org|access-date=2023-03-07|archive-date=2023-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307120620/https://www.ieice.org/eng/about_ieice/new_honorary_members_award_winners/2017/meiyo_04e.html|url-status=live}}</ref> a Fellow of the [[Japan Society of Applied Physics|Japan Society of Applied Physics (JSAP)]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jsap.or.jp/english/awards/jsap-fellow/recipients4 |title=4th JSAP Fellow (2010) &#124; |access-date=2023-03-08 |archive-date=2023-03-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308082600/https://www.jsap.or.jp/english/awards/jsap-fellow/recipients4 |url-status=live }}</ref> a Life Fellow of [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]],<ref name="ieee">{{Cite web |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37273573700 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2023-03-07 |archive-date=2022-09-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220913070230/https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37273573700 |url-status=live }}</ref> and a Fellow Emeritus, [[Optica (society)|OPTICA]] (formerly OSA).<ref name="osa">{{Cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/en-us/history/biographies/bios/masataka_nakazawa/|title=Masataka Nakazawa &#124; Living History &#124; Optica|website=www.optica.org|access-date=2023-03-07|archive-date=2023-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307120620/https://www.optica.org/en-us/history/biographies/bios/masataka_nakazawa/|url-status=live}}</ref> He also served as a Director at Large of the Optical Society of America (OSA) in 2007,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/en-us/about/newsroom/news_releases/2007/vicepresident/|title=OSA Elects 2008 Vice President, James C. Wyant &#124; News Releases &#124; Optica|website=www.optica.org|access-date=2023-03-08|archive-date=2023-03-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308082559/https://www.optica.org/en-us/about/newsroom/news_releases/2007/vicepresident/|url-status=live}}</ref> on the Board of Governors of the IEEE Photonics Society in 2013,<ref name="ieee" /> and as the President of IEICE in 2019<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieice.org/eng_r/about/president_list.html|title=President List &#124; IEICE The Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers|website=www.ieice.org|access-date=2023-03-08|archive-date=2023-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230401012614/https://www.ieice.org/eng_r/about/president_list.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
